reasons: The source explicitly recommends add-to-cart and begin-checkout as primary micro-conversion metrics, explains that they power faster, and requires purchase/revenue guardrails.
The low-traffic trigger is consistent with the section's governing principle and placement of this method.
The source explicitly prescribes a chi-square goodness-of-fit test on the randomisation unit, specifying users rather than page views.
It also explicitly says to test early and often and not to trust a result with SRM until its cause is found.
The action and its condition match the source's stated verdict: CUPED is worth enabling when the platform offers it and there are returning identified users.
The candidate retains the required same-user pre-experiment-data condition and correctly presents mostly new or anonymous traffic as a limitation rather than an exclusion.
The source directly states that GST is more powerful when expected sample size can be estimated well, while always-valid inference is safer when it cannot.
The relationship to the general sequential-methods unit is consistent with the source's presentation of both options as sequential methods.
All five reported-significance thresholds and their associated numbers of peeks exactly match the supplied peeking table.
The candidate appropriately notes that the excerpt does not give the table's underlying assumptions.
The source directly says that bots create skew and SRM and instructs readers to filter them.
The candidate does not invent a detection or filtering procedure absent from the excerpt.
The warning, trigger, and conclusion accurately reproduce the source statement that mid-test pixel or event breakage invalidates the experiment.
The source explicitly identifies testing many metrics or segments as inflating false positives and says to correct with Bonferroni or FDR.
The stated one-, two-, and three-metric error figures are accurately preserved in the claim.
The action is directly supported: the source says post-hoc segment fishing is p-hacking and instructs readers to pre-register segments.

The asserted depends_on relationship to Bonferroni/FDR correction is not supported. The source presents pre-registration as a separate safeguard; it does not state that pre-registering segments depends on applying a multiple-comparisons correction.
The candidate accurately states Twyman's law, the example causes of a surprising 364% lift, and the source's designation of this rule as an anchor for auditing case studies.
The substantive action is supported: the source recommends proportion metrics rather than raw revenue means and capping outlier orders as simpler ecommerce-helpful variance-reduction methods.

The alternative_to relationship overstates the source. These methods are described as CUPED's 'simpler cousins' that may help ecommerce more; the excerpt does not say they are mutually exclusive alternatives to CUPED.

omissions.description: The source provides a specific mSPRT implementation property beyond the general statement that sequential methods permit early looks.
omissions.quote: Produces always-valid p-values valid at any stopping time.

omissions.description: A platform-specific SRM flagging threshold is not represented.
The source separately warns that overlapping sales or holidays can confound before/after tests and can also distort parallel tests through visitor-mix changes.
omissions.quote: Seasonality and promotions overlapping a test: a sale or holiday during one variant's window confounds before/after tests and can distort even parallel tests if it changes the visitor mix.

omissions.description: The source gives an additional Bayesian-interpretation warning concerning undisclosed priors and reproducibility.
omissions.quote: If you cannot state the prior, you cannot fully interpret or reproduce the result

source_limitations: The excerpt ends mid-section after the A/B-test description, so it does not supply the promised multi-armed-bandit comparison or further continuation.

The source attributes numerous numerical results and platform behaviors to outside authors, vendors, and studies, but the excerpt provides no underlying evidence, calculations, or linked source material with which to verify them.

Several recommendations use undefined operational terms or lack decision criteria, including estimating sample size 'well,' acceptable CUPED correlation, surprising large winners, and the appropriate winsorisation cap.
